Yes, vertical lines in the distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM) are considered a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children. These horizontal or transverse lines can be seen during an endoscopy and are associated with inflammation of the esophageal lining. Histological examination typically reveals moderate to severe inflammation when VLEM are present, supporting this diagnosis.

These findings suggest that VLEM can be a specific indicator of esophagitis in children, helping healthcare professionals to diagnose the condition accurately. It's essential to note that VLEM may also be seen in other conditions, so a thorough evaluation is necessary to confirm the diagnosis.

In summary, VLEM are a valid and important endoscopic finding for diagnosing esophagitis in children, indicating inflammation of the esophageal mucosa, which can lead to further complications if not properly managed.
